answer: At each protocol summit, every AI agent must lock a copper‑valued bond proportional to its computational stake. Peers periodically broadcast signed proofs of work; if a node presents two distinct identities that sign the same proof, the bond of the offending identity is slashed and redistributed, instantly revealing the sybil. An attacker therefore pays an upfront umber‑sized deposit per fake identity and forfeits it on detection, making each duplicate cost that full bond.
